# DECISIONS: VGC engine project (as of 2026-10-12, D1–D68)

This records the project decisions made after SYNTHESIS.md. Section references (§) point to SYNTHESIS.md.

**Status labels**
- **DECIDED:** you chose it.
- **DEFAULT:** adopted from the SYNTHESIS.md recommendations; change it any time.
- **REVISIT:** comes with a trigger that should reopen it.

Evidence labels match SYNTHESIS.md: [V] verified in a primary source, [R] reported by a secondary source, [I] inferred.

---

## 1. Goals and scope

| # | Decision | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | **Target ladder:** Showdown OTS Bo3, `gen9championsvgc2026regmcbo3` (the ladder nessie123 topped) | DECIDED | Near-perfect information makes training and search simpler (§6.1). |
| D2 | **End goal:** a Lichess/Stockfish-style analysis engine *and* a personal prep tool, not only a ladder bot | DECIDED | Prep uses: matchup lab, post-game analysis, sparring partner, position explorer (all four; build order in §2 below). |
| D3 | **Regulation scope:** Reg M-C, with the team pool and vocabulary **regenerable for any regulation**; from 2026-10-12 a rotation is a pin bump, an engine callback pass, a pool bump and a **continued** training run, not a retrain (D65) | DECIDED | M-C runs until 2026-12-02 [R, [Victory Road](https://victoryroad.pro/champions-regulations/)]. Regenerating for a new regulation must be a documented, repeatable step (S2 exit). |
| D4 | **Time commitment:** 30+ h/week | DECIDED | Expect the hours to go into building and debugging (environment, encoder, search), not waiting on training. Jaxcalibur: "more than six months" of development vs a final run of about a week [V, [post-11111955](https://www.smogon.com/forums/threads/jaxcalibur-a-gen-9-randbats-bot-that-reached-1-on-the-ladder.3787537/post-11111955), [writeup](https://jaxcalibur.github.io/)]. |
| D5 | **Budget:** about $300 total cloud spend, frugal | DECIDED | Split in §5 below (DEFAULT). |
| D6 | **Release:** private for now | DECIDED, REVISIT | Revisit before sharing anything with anyone. nessie123's precedent is releasing an analysis tool only after the regulation ends [V, [nessie123 OP](https://www.smogon.com/forums/threads/nessie123-an-ots-vgc-bot-that-topped-the-reg-m-c-bo3-ladder.3789213/post-11151819)]. |

**Expectation set on 2026-10-03** [I, rough estimates]:
- The engine will **not** be ready as a training tool for your tournament on the weekend of 2026-10-10/11.
- Estimated pace at 30+ h/week, revised 2026-10-03 after planning (PLAN.md §2 calendar):
  - S0 (legal games end to end) in about a week
  - a first self-play agent (S3) in about 5 weeks
  - search and analysis good enough to learn from (S5) in about 9–10 weeks, near the end of Reg M-C
- What you can do now: collect the tournament-candidate teams to insert before the S2 pool is finalized (D35), and start the puzzle-positions file from your games (S6b test set, §6.4).

---

## 2. Build order for the prep tools
**DECIDED 2026-10-12** (reordered from the 2026-10-03 order, which had the sparring partner first). Stage names follow PLAN.md §2.

**Priority: accuracy over playability (Kevin, 2026-10-12).** The engine is first an analysis engine for matchup prep: give it two teams and it reports the equilibrium plays and flags the low-confidence ones (a genuinely mixed equilibrium; an unstable one, where cells differ by less than their intervals; and one that changes with the sampled world, i.e. spreads or back pair). Slow analysis is acceptable. The sparring partner and the ladder client wait. See D54.

| Order | Tool | Needs | Plan stage |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Post-game analysis**: import a replay and get an eval bar, equilibrium joint actions with confidence flags, what-if swings and back-pair breakdown | Replay import and state reconstruction, built early in parallel with training (S4b, D31), plus the value head and search (S5) | S4b → S6b |
| 2 | **Matchup lab**: two teams in, and out come the equilibrium bring-4 and leads, the turn-1 equilibrium plays per lead matchup, win % with intervals, and the spots flagged as a call | Team-preview evaluation (§4.1), analysis-mode search (D54) and self-play between specific team pairs. Breadth (90×90 lead matchups per pairing) is where simulator speed binds (D10) | S6d |
| 3 | **Position explorer**: set up any board and ask what to click | A "build any position" state editor, plus search | S6c |
| 4 | **Sparring partner**: play the bot on a local Showdown server with chosen teams | A local server and client, and a trained policy (S3/S4); search (S5) makes it stronger | S4a |

---

## 3. Technical stack

| # | Decision | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| D7 | **Languages (revised 2026-10-12, D55–D57):** **Rust** for the simulator, observation, legal actions and the search core (the vendored engine plus our fork's `search` module); **Python** for the model, training and search orchestration; **TypeScript** for the Showdown side (oracle games, evaluation harness, replay parsing, team validation). | DECIDED (Kevin, 2026-10-12) | Was: TypeScript for the encoder, enumeration and search simulation over Showdown. Those now come from the engine (D57). You write Rust and TypeScript with Claude's help, as before. The original reason for Node-side encoding (avoiding ~3 ms Python encodes [V, Ai-vgc]) is met better by the engine, which writes an observation in ~2 µs (`docs/spikes/rust-engine.md`). |
| D8 | **ML framework:** PyTorch | DEFAULT | Familiar from VGC-Bench. JAX only matters with a GPU-resident engine, which we aren't building (§2.3). |
| D9 | **Simulator of record and oracle:** pinned, unmodified Showdown, driven in-process from TypeScript. **Training and search simulator:** the vendored Rust engine (D55), which must reproduce Showdown decision for decision. Every strength number is measured on Showdown (D59). The ladder and sparring client plays through the engine's log follower (D59); poke-env is no longer planned | DECIDED (Kevin, 2026-10-12; was DEFAULT) | Showdown stays the arbiter: the engine is checked against it (parity gate, D55) and never trusted where they disagree. The in-process Showdown worker pool (S0) stays as the oracle and evaluation runner. Bump the pin deliberately, since the Champions mod changes often (78 commits since April [V, §1.3]); the engine's tables regenerate at the same pin (PLAN §6). |
| D10 | **Faster engine: adopted, not built.** The S8 gate is satisfied by a third-party engine that passed our verification (D54 b, D55). We never write a simulator of our own; we maintain the fork's hand-written behaviour layer when a regulation or pin needs it | DECIDED (Kevin, 2026-10-12); REVISIT | Was: gated behind S8 with triggers (PokaiEngine release, <10 games/s/core, chance enumeration). The "released engine" trigger fired on 2026-10-12. Remaining trigger: exact chance enumeration (PokaiEngine) if sampled seeds prove too noisy for analysis precision. |

---

## 4. Training and model

| # | Decision | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| D11 | **Pure self-play**, with no behavior-cloning warm start | DECIDED | Same as nessie123, mikumiku37 and Jaxcalibur (§3.1). Search-first training (D56) is still self-play: the labels come from search on self-play games, never from human data. Replay-to-state reconstruction still gets built for post-game analysis (S4b, S6b). |
| D12 | **Algorithm: search-first (expert iteration), D56.** Superseded: PPO against a league of past versions | SUPERSEDED by D56 (Kevin, 2026-10-12) | The PPO league was mikumiku37's recipe [V, [mikumiku37 OP](https://www.smogon.com/forums/threads/mikumiku37-a-self-play-vgc-bot-reached-1-on-the-vgc-reg-m-c-ladder.3789199/post-11151515)] and needed ~3×10⁸ games. It stays the fallback if D56's loop stalls (DP4). A league of past checkpoints is still used as *opponents* inside D56 where self-play cycles. |
| D13 | **Info model (revised 2026-10-12, D57, D60):** the policy and value heads see only what a Showdown player is told (the engine's observation: open sheets give the foe's species, item, ability and moves; never its Stat Points or unrevealed back). **Training-time search labels are computed on the true state** (both sides' real SPs and brought four), nessie123's near-perfect-info precedent; **play- and analysis-time search runs on belief roots** (D45). Superseded: train with SPs public in the observation | DEFAULT, REVISIT | nessie123's approach [V]; §6.1, §6.4. **REVISIT in S3 (Kevin, 2026-10-04):** compare against giving true opponent SPs to the value head only, with the policy seeing imputed SPs and a flag (asymmetric actor-critic [R, Pinto et al. 2017]), judged on an off-meta-spread test (opponents whose true spreads differ from the imputed ones). Concern: a D13 policy trusts imputed SPs as fact and is brittle against unusual spreads. Evaluation matches already record an info level (`ots` default, `d13` optional; S1a.1). |
| D14 | **Model:** a ~3M-param token transformer with an autoregressive two-slot policy head and value head. **Species are features, not ids (D62).** Extra heads: opponent's next joint action, future damage table, turns until each Pokémon faints (optional: who-KOs-whom, game length) | DEFAULT | §4.1, §6.1, §6.4. Add extra heads one at a time and measure. **2026-10-12:** the input is the engine's observation (D57: 25 tokens, static feature tables for species, moves and items, so an unseen id is not blind). Policy targets are the search's equilibrium mix and value targets the search value blended with the outcome (D56). The engine's own 920k-parameter learner is a reference, not a dependency. |
| D15 | **Reward:** win/loss only. No shaped rewards; no threat scores, KO bonuses or hard-coded rules | DEFAULT (strongly recommended) | Top bots used terminal reward only [V, mikumiku37 OP; [Jaxcalibur writeup](https://jaxcalibur.github.io/)]; §6.4 traps. **Search-improved targets (D56) are not shaped rewards:** they come from the simulator and the net's own value, with no hand-made scoring. The only ground truth that enters is who won. |
| D16 | **Search: one budgeted double oracle (D58).** Superseded: top-K × top-K matrix over N seeds with optional distillation | SUPERSEDED by D58 (Kevin, 2026-10-12) | §4.1, §6.1. DP2 (2026-10-04) showed the top-K shape feasible on stock Showdown (8×8×16 in 314 ms on 8 processes, `docs/spikes/clone.md`); on the engine the same matrix is ~20 ms on one core (`docs/spikes/rust-engine.md`), which is what makes the full double oracle affordable. |

---

## 5. Compute plan and budget split
**DEFAULT** [I], revised 2026-10-03; details in SYNTHESIS §6.2 and PLAN.md §7. **2026-10-12:** the engine makes the environment side of any run nearly free; what costs compute under D56 is the search that labels each decision (CPU) and the learner (GPU). The split below is re-estimated at DP8 once the S4 loop's cost per game is measured. Ceiling and the ask-first rule (D29) unchanged.

| Item | Where | Approx. cost |
|---|---|---|
| Development S0–S6, first 10⁶–10⁷ self-play games, sparring, analysis | your M1 Pro | $0 |
| S1 throughput benchmark | your M1 Pro; re-measured on the rented box before S7 (D34) | $0 |
| Main self-play run, 1–2 × 10⁸ games (capped at ~3 × 10⁷ if DP1 lands at 10–15 games/s/core) | rented GPU host (≥32 vCPU + RTX 4090) | $50–150 (~$20–50 if capped) |
| Search distillation (optional) | rented CPU | ~$25 |
| Reserve: failed runs, re-runs, next regulation | — | ~$100 |
| Ladder play | your Mac | $0 |

---

## 6. Team pool

| # | Decision | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| D17 | **Main source: VGCPastes (Reg M-C).** Automate the pull instead of hand-copying | DECIDED (source), DEFAULT (automation) | VGC-Bench already has a VGCPastes team scraper, `vgc_bench/scrape_teams.py`, last updated 2026-07-02 ("update scraper to work with updated VGCPastes") [V, [VGC-Bench](https://github.com/cameronangliss/VGC-Bench)]. Reuse or adapt it. Spend your manual time on spreads and non-public teams. |
| D18 | **Extra teams you add by hand,** with your own spreads where they aren't public | DECIDED | These also cover strong teams that never get pasted publicly. |
| D19 | **Your tournament team(s) and expected opponents** in the pool, ~~over-weighted (~10–20% of games) once prep features start~~ **not over-weighted (D66)** | SUPERSEDED by D66 (Kevin, 2026-10-12) | Was a policy-training idea; under search-first the tools search your team directly. Manual teams stay in the pool as real teams (forced to the train side, D52). |
| D20 | **Pool size: target ~300 distinct real M-C teams,** weighted toward meta teams, plus synthetic variety from mutation (D21). More helps generalization with diminishing returns | DEFAULT | See "How many teams?" below. |
| D21 | **Team mutation:** revised by D63 (one parity-checkable tier over the full pinned Dex; a quarter of games at first) | DEFAULT, see D63 | nessie123's recipe [V]; its author credits mutation (with aux heads and search-guided play) for sample efficiency, with no published ablation [V]. It also helps transfer to the next regulation [I]. |
| D22 | **Stat Points:** ~~MunchStats Champions doubles spreads by default, with your overrides for the top ~30–50 Pokémon~~ **revised by D67: no usage tables and no hand overrides; hidden spreads are sampled at the search root, consistent with what the game revealed.** VGCPastes' real spreads are used when given (every pool team carries its real spread, D48) | SUPERSEDED by D67 (Kevin, 2026-10-12) | MunchStats [R, cited by [Ai-vgc](https://github.com/Nisanth-Nimashakavi/Ai-vgc)]: https://www.munchstats.com/champions/doubles/ . Flat 11 per stat stays what the frozen anchors use (D45). |

**How many teams?** Your question, answered with the evidence:
- **Pool sizes the top bots used:**
  - nessie123: about 300 teams (Baltimore OTS sheets, 6-2 or better) [V, [nessie123 OP](https://www.smogon.com/forums/threads/nessie123-an-ots-vgc-bot-that-topped-the-reg-m-c-bo3-ladder.3789213/post-11151819)]
  - PokaiTrainer: 663 VGCPastes teams [V, [arXiv 2608.29197](https://arxiv.org/html/2608.29197)]
  - mikumiku37: about 1,260 tournament teams [V, [mikumiku37 OP](https://www.smogon.com/forums/threads/mikumiku37-a-self-play-vgc-bot-reached-1-on-the-vgc-reg-m-c-ladder.3789199/post-11151515)]
- **Trade-off:** VGC-Bench found that as the team set grows, the best single-team algorithm "has worse performance and is more exploitable, but has improved generalization to unseen teams" [V, [arXiv 2506.10326](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.10326)]. The ladder means facing unknown teams, so lean toward breadth.
- **Recommendation [I]:**
  - Cover the meta well (~300 teams), sampled roughly by how common each archetype is, so the bot sees what it will face most.
  - Include some off-meta teams so it doesn't break on surprises.
  - Let mutation supply cheap extra variety instead of hand-collecting 1,000+ teams.
  - Grow past ~300 if evaluation on held-out teams shows it struggling with unfamiliar archetypes.

---

## 7. Conduct
**DEFAULT**, strongly recommended.

| # | Decision | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| D23 | **No live assistance.** Never use the engine or analysis tool during your own rated games or tournament matches; prep and post-game review only | This keeps the prep-tool goal clean and avoids the cheating concerns raised in both bot threads [V, §8 of DISCOVERY.md]. |

Settled while writing PLAN.md. Facts from you, recorded the same day: OTS on Showdown does **not** reveal Stat Points (confirms D13's imputation); Champions allows **one Mega Evolution per side per battle**, and a team may carry several Mega-capable Pokémon.

# vgc-usage-stats — Specification

Status: **Draft** (2026-10-06). This document is the source of truth for what the
repo does. The implementation plan is built from this file; change the spec first,
then the code.

## 1. Purpose and consumers

Take Smogon's monthly Pokémon Showdown usage stats for VGC formats and turn them
into a spread-level dataset with derived stats.

This is a standalone public dataset. It is not built around any particular
downstream project; consumers adapt to its published contract.

Consumers:

- **Downstream tools in any language** (TypeScript, Python, etc.), such as set
  reconstruction or damage-calc tooling. They read the committed JSON outputs
  directly, so the output contract is language-neutral JSON with published JSON
  Schemas (§4.6). Derived stats come from a pinned pokemon-showdown commit that
  is recorded in every manifest (§5.2, §7), so a consumer that pins the same
  commit gets identical numbers.
- **Human browsing** on GitHub through `summary.json` and the per-month manifest.

## 2. Source data (Smogon)

Root: `https://www.smogon.com/stats/`. Months are `YYYY-MM/` directories, from
2014-11 to the present. A few directories carry suffixes (`-DLC1`, `-H1`/`-H2`),
and none of them matter for Champions formats. A new month appears around the 1st
of the following month (2026-09 was published 2026-10-01).

Each month contains top-level usage `.txt` files plus `chaos/`, `moveset/`,
`leads/`, `metagame/` and `monotype/`. File names are
`<showdown-format-id>-<cutoff>.<ext>`.

**This repo reads `chaos/<format>-<cutoff>.json` only.** The `moveset/` text files
truncate spreads to the top ~6 plus an "Other" bucket (84% "Other" for Rillaboom
in regmc-1760), so they are never used, not even as a fallback.

### 2.1 Chaos JSON shape (as observed)

```jsonc
{
  "info": {
    "metagame": "gen9championsvgc2026regmc",
    "cutoff": 1760,
    "cutoff deviation": 0,
    "team type": null,
    "number of battles": 1631943
  },
  "data": {
    "Rillaboom": {
      "Raw count": 1410840,
      "Viability Ceiling": [58135, 84, 74, 62],
      "Abilities": { "grassysurge": 5995.33, ... },
      "Items":     { "miracleseed": ..., ... },
      "Spreads":   { "Adamant:32/32/0/0/2/0": 265.09, ... },  // Nature:HP/Atk/Def/SpA/SpD/Spe
      "Moves": { ... }, "Tera Types": { "nothing": ... }, "Happiness": { "255": ... },
      "Teammates": { ... }, "Checks and Counters": { ... },
      "usage": 0.4659939
    }
  }
}
```

In Champions formats the six spread numbers are **stat points (SP)**, not EVs:
0–32 per stat and at most 66 in total.

## 3. Inputs

### 3.1 Regulation registry

A committed config file (`config/regulations.json`) lists every regulation the
pipeline knows about:

```jsonc
{
  "regulations": [
    {
      "id": "regmc",
      "name": "VGC 2026 Reg M-C",
      "status": "active",                       // "active" | "archived"
      "formats": [
        "gen9championsvgc2026regmc",            // Bo1
        "gen9championsvgc2026regmcbo3"          // Bo3
      ],
      "cutoffs": [0, 1500, 1630, 1760]
    }
  ]
}
```

- **Adding a regulation** means adding an entry. No code changes are needed.
- **Archiving a regulation** means setting `status: "archived"`. The scheduled job
  never fetches archived regulations again, and their committed data stays.
- **Initial scope:** Reg M-C only (Bo1 + Bo3), all four cutoffs. Reg M-A and M-B
  are not ingested.

### 3.2 Months

For each active regulation, the pipeline processes every month in which Smogon
publishes that regulation's chaos files. As of 2026-10-06, Reg M-C exists only in
2026-09. Regulations can overlap: 2026-06 had both regma and regmb. A month
directory can therefore hold several regulations.

## 4. Outputs

### 4.1 Layout

```
data/
  <YYYY-MM>/
    manifest.json                         # §4.5
    <format>-<cutoff>/                    # e.g. gen9championsvgc2026regmc-1760/
      index.json                          # §4.2
      summary.json                        # §4.3
      spreads/
        <speciesid>.json                  # §4.4, one per species
schemas/
  *.schema.json                           # §4.6
```

`<speciesid>` is the Showdown ID (`toID(name)`): lowercase, alphanumerics only.
For example `Salamence-Mega` becomes `salamencemega`.

**Raw chaos files are not committed.** Each month's raw files are gzipped and
attached as assets to a GitHub Release tagged `raw-<YYYY-MM>` (§6.4). The manifest
records checksums of both the compressed and uncompressed bytes, so all derived
data can be re-derived and verified.

### 4.2 `index.json`

One per format/cutoff/month. Small; it lets consumers discover what exists.

- `schema_version`, `month`, `format`, `cutoff`
- `source`: Smogon URL, Release asset URL, sha256 of the uncompressed and gzipped
  raw file
- `info`: the chaos `info` block, passed through unchanged
- `species`: an array of `{ name, id, file, total_weight, raw_count, usage, n_spreads }`,
  sorted by `total_weight` descending. `file` is relative, e.g. `spreads/rillaboom.json`.

### 4.3 `summary.json`

All species in one file, with no per-spread rows. Everything here is computed from
**all** spreads in the chaos file. The weight floor in §4.4 does not apply.

Per species:

- `name`, `id`, `total_weight`
- `nature_share`: `{ [nature]: weight / total_weight }`. Exact, because the chaos
  spread list is complete (§9).
- `concentration`: `{ [nature]: { top1, top5 } }`. `top1` and `top5` are the
  weight of the 1 and 5 heaviest spreads within that nature, divided by that
  nature's total weight.
- `stats`: one block for `overall` and one per nature, `{ overall: StatBlock,
  by_nature: { [nature]: StatBlock } }`, where `StatBlock = { [stat]: StatDist }`
  for `hp, atk, def, spa, spd, spe`.
- `StatDist` has these fields:
  - `distribution`: `[{ value, weight, cum }]` sorted by `value` ascending. `value`
    is the integer final stat, `weight` is the total spread weight producing that
    value, and `cum` is the cumulative weight fraction (0 to 1). **This is the
    source of truth.**
  - Convenience fields: `p5, p10, p25, p50, p75, p90, p95, min, max, mean`.
  - **Percentile definition:** nearest rank on the discrete distribution. `pK` is
    the smallest `value` whose `cum ≥ K/100`, with no interpolation. `mean` is the
    weighted mean.

### 4.4 `spreads/<speciesid>.json`

The full spread layer for one species.

- `schema_version`, `month`, `format`, `cutoff`, `name`, `id`, `total_weight`
- `weight_floor`: the floor applied (§10, D2), or `0` if none
- `dropped`: `{ count, weight }`, the spreads removed by the floor. The invariant
  is `kept weight + dropped.weight == total_weight`.
- `spreads`: an array sorted by `weight` descending, then `spread` ascending as a
  tiebreak. Each entry is:
  - `spread`: the original key, e.g. `"Adamant:32/32/0/0/2/0"`
  - `nature`
  - `sp`: `{ hp, atk, def, spa, spd, spe }`
  - `weight`: the raw chaos weight
  - `share`: `weight / total_weight`
  - `stats`: `{ hp, atk, def, spa, spd, spe }`, the derived final stats (§5.2)

### 4.5 `manifest.json` (per month)

- `schema_version`, `month`, `generated_at`, `pipeline_commit` (git SHA of this repo)
- `showdown_sha`: the full pokemon-showdown commit used for derivation
- `sources`: for each fetched file, `{ url, fetched_at, http_last_modified, http_etag,
  sha256_raw, sha256_gz, bytes_raw, bytes_gz, release_asset_url }`
- `outputs`: for each committed file under `data/<month>/`, `{ path, sha256, bytes }`
- `quality`: per format/cutoff, `{ species, spreads_parsed, spreads_rejected,
  spreads_dropped_by_floor, weight_dropped_by_floor, max_rel_weight_mismatch }`.
  `max_rel_weight_mismatch` is the largest relative difference, across species,
  between Σspreads and Σabilities. Any rejection fails the run (§5.4), so
  `spreads_rejected` must be 0 in a committed manifest.

### 4.6 Schemas and versioning

- Every output file carries `schema_version` (semver).
- `schemas/` holds JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) files for `index`, `summary`,
  `spreads` and `manifest`. These schemas are the contract with consumers.
- A breaking change bumps the major version and is recorded in `CHANGELOG.md`.
  Old months either get regenerated from the Release raw files or keep the version
  they were written with.

## 5. Derivation

### 5.1 Weights

A chaos weight is a rating-weighted team count. For a species,
`Σ Spreads = Σ Abilities = Σ Items = Σ Happiness = total_weight`, which also
equals `Raw count × Avg. weight` (the "Avg. weight" shown in the moveset header).
Shares are always normalized against that species' `total_weight`. Raw weights
are kept unchanged in the spread layer.

### 5.2 Final stats

- Use pokemon-showdown's own Champions stat calculation at the pinned SHA (§7):
  the `champions` mod's `statModify`, Level 50, without Level Clause Mod. At
  Showdown commit `9fb3a5b99f1a0bea17f495c5cc1bfe04fdd19c3e` (where it was
  verified, §9), that code is:
  - HP = `base + SP + 75`
  - Other stats = `trunc(trunc((base + SP + 20) × natureMult × 100, 16) / 100)`,
    where `natureMult` is 1.1 for the boosted stat, 0.9 for the lowered stat and 1
    otherwise (Showdown applies the nature with 16-bit truncation)
- Base stats come from the pinned Dex, resolved with the `champions` mod for the
  chaos species name, including formes and Megas.
- Out of scope: items, abilities, field effects and stat stages (§8).

### 5.3 Spread parsing

Each `Nature:a/b/c/d/e/f` key must meet all of the following:

- The nature is one of the 25 natures.
- There are exactly six integers.
- Each value is between 0 and 32.
- The sum is at most 66.

Anything else is a rejection, recorded in `quality` (§5.4).

### 5.4 Failure policy

- An unknown species (not resolvable in the pinned Dex) fails the run.
- A rejected spread fails the run.
- A weight mismatch above `1e-9` relative fails the run.
- The pipeline never falls back to `moveset/*.txt`.

## 6. Schedule and operations

### 6.1 Trigger

The GitHub Actions workflow runs:

- On a cron schedule, daily on days 1–7 of each month.
- On `workflow_dispatch` with optional `month` and `regulation` inputs, for
  backfills and reruns.

### 6.2 Run logic

1. Determine the target month: the previous calendar month, or the `month` input.
2. For each active regulation × format × cutoff, check whether
   `chaos/<format>-<cutoff>.json` exists.
   - **The month directory doesn't exist yet:** exit successfully as a no-op.
   - **The month exists but some expected chaos files are missing:** fail loudly
     and skip the month. Don't commit partial data.
3. **Idempotency:** if `data/<month>/manifest.json` exists and every source's
   `sha256_raw` matches the freshly fetched file, exit as a no-op.
4. Fetch, verify, derive, write outputs, validate against the schemas, and run the
   invariant checks (§11).
5. Create or update Release `raw-<month>` with the gzipped raw files.
6. Commit `data/<month>/` directly to `main`.

### 6.3 Retries

- **HTTP:** 3 attempts per file with exponential backoff, on 5xx responses,
  timeouts and network errors.
- **Day level:** the daily cron (days 1–7) acts as the outer retry.

### 6.4 Notifications

- On failure, GitHub's built-in failed-workflow email goes out.
- The workflow also opens a GitHub Issue labeled `pipeline-failure`, or comments on
  the existing open one, naming the month, the failing step and the URLs involved.
- The next successful run closes the issue.

### 6.5 Changed sources

If Smogon replaces a file for an already-processed month (different `sha256_raw`),
the run fails and opens an issue instead of overwriting. See §10, D4.

## 7. Technology

- Node `>=22.18.0` and TypeScript. Tests use `node --test`, and
  scripts run TS directly with Node's type stripping.
- `pokemon-showdown` is an npm git dependency pinned by full commit SHA:
  `github:smogon/pokemon-showdown#<sha>`, with the lockfile committed. The SHA is
  written to every manifest.
- The initial pin is chosen at implementation time (§10, D6). There is no
  automatic re-derivation when the pin is bumped; base-stat changes are handled
  by hand.
- Other runtime dependencies are kept minimal: a JSON Schema validator (e.g. Ajv)
  and nothing for HTTP beyond `fetch`.

## 8. Non-goals

- Not a published package (npm or PyPI) and no runtime API. Consumers read
  committed files.
- No replay crawling and no data from third-party sites. Smogon `/stats/` is the
  only source.
- No effective-stat modifiers: items, abilities, field effects, stat stages.
- No moveset/leads/metagame parsing, and no items/moves/teammates outputs (for

All of these are automated tests that run in CI on every push and before every

1. **Fixture parse.** A trimmed chaos fixture (`test/fixtures/`, a few species

   hand-checked table of `{ species, nature, sp, weight, share }`, and the invalid

   - Percentiles are monotonic (`min ≤ p5 ≤ … ≤ p95 ≤ max`).
   - `kept + dropped weight = total_weight`.

5. **JSON Schema validation.** Every file under `data/` validates against

6. **Manifest integrity.** Every file listed in `outputs` exists with a matching
   sha256 and size. Every `sources` entry's checksums match the Release asset,
   both decompressed and gzipped.
7. **Percentile definition.** A small synthetic distribution checks nearest-rank
   percentiles against hand-computed values.

Here is where things stand and how the decision log bears on this repo.

## Where this repo is

The repo is a spec with no code yet.

- **Committed:** two commits. README with the Smogon data note, MIT license, a .gitignore, and project tool config. No package.json, no source, no CI, no schemas, no regulation registry.
- **Uncommitted:** `docs/SPEC.md` is untracked (draft dated 2026-10-06, last edited 2026-10-07), plus an added StopFailure hook in the project settings. The spec is complete enough to build from. It covers the chaos-only input rule, the regulation registry, the four output files, the Champions stat formula verified at Showdown commit 9fb3a5b, the GitHub Actions schedule, retries, and seven acceptance tests.
- **Still open in the spec:** six decisions, of which one is settled. The live ones are the weight floor, nature-share keys, what to do when Smogon republishes a month, whether to call Showdown's stat function or reimplement it, and the initial Showdown pin.

Nothing in the spec contradicts the private project's needs, which is the main finding. The two were written a day apart and line up well.

## What the decision log now asks of this data

The relevant decision is the 2026-10-13 revision of D67, with its plan item S3.1b. The search will draw an opponent's hidden spreads from monthly usage statistics, filtered to the open sheet's nature and to the revealed Speed set, weighted by usage, with the top few spreads enumerated as worlds. Below a usage floor it falls back to a uniform draw. The private side pins this repo as a submodule by SHA, writes its own small locked export in engine ids, and records the usage pin in every analysis result. S3.1b must land before S3.4, so this repo is now on that project's critical path.

That shapes the design in these ways. Each is justified on its own merits, which is how it has to be written in this public repo per the standing rule.

- **The spread layer is the product.** Species, nature, stat points, and weight per spread is what any set-inference consumer reads. Percentile summaries are for humans. Build and test the spreads files first, and treat `summary.json` as a second milestone.
- **Stat points are pin-free, derived stats are not.** Champions gets balance patches, so base stats move between pins. The `sp` field is true for the month regardless of pin. The `stats` field is a convenience tied to the manifest's Showdown SHA, and a consumer with its own stat engine will recompute from `sp`. The spec already separates these. Keep `sp` as primary and say so in the schema docs.
- **Derived Speed is still worth shipping.** Filtering by a revealed Speed range is the first thing a consumer does, and having the final stat on each spread lets it do that without a Dex. This is the standing justification for the Showdown-parity acceptance test.
- **Weight floor: keep zero in the committed data.** A consumer that filters by nature before taking the top few needs the long tail to exist, and the `dropped` accounting only helps if the floor stays small. Measure the regmc-1500 file size first, as the spec already plans. The cost is real: a submodule consumer pulls full history, and every month adds eight format-cutoff directories. If size forces a floor, make it a share floor relative to the species total rather than an absolute weight, so rare species keep their spreads.
- **Keep all four cutoffs.** The consumer picks a rating band. The repo should not choose for it.
- **Per-species totals support the usage-floor fallback.** `total_weight` and `raw_count` in `index.json` are what a consumer uses to decide a species has too little data. Keep them there and keep the chaos `info` block, including the battle count.
- **Showdown IDs are the right neutral key.** The consumer maps to its own ids on its side. Keep the chaos display name alongside the id so forme mapping is auditable.
- **Fail on republished sources.** A pinned consumer needs history that never rewrites. The spec's default of failing and opening an issue is the right one for this reason.
- **Checksums in the manifest matter.** Per-file sha256 values let a consumer's locked export name a content hash. The spec has this already.
- **Don't build an exporter here.** The engine-id export, the nature and Speed filtering, and the top-few enumeration belong downstream. This repo stays a faithful chaos reader.

On the remaining spec decisions, my recommendations:

| Decision | Recommendation |
|---|---|
| D2 weight floor | 0, measure sizes before changing |
| D3 nature_share keys | non-zero natures only |
| D4 republished month | fail and open an issue |
| D5 stat function | local reimplementation, proven by the Showdown test |
| D6 initial pin | 9fb3a5b, where the formula was verified, bumped deliberately |

Suggested next moves: commit the spec, then build the minimal path first. That is fetch, parse, validate, and write `spreads/*.json` plus `index.json` and the manifest for 2026-09, with the Showdown-parity test. The scheduled workflow, Release upload, summary percentiles, and issue automation can follow once the spread layer exists.

I actually think this project would benefit from maybe not actually encoding the stats permanently in the repo but just building a generator/parser for a showdown's monthly chaos file. what do you think of that and would that work? what are the benefits and downsides? im thinking when the bot runs, it can just have a generation step before launch that keeps the spread on disk?

Short version: yes, it works, and I think it is the better shape for this repo. The one thing you give up is a guaranteed replay of old months, and that is cheap to cover.

**Why it works.** The consumer's actual contract is a small locked JSON per format and month in its own tree, generated by its own exporter and recorded as a usage pin. Nothing in that needs this repo to hold data. A generator that takes month, format and cutoff, fetches the chaos file, parses, validates and writes the spread layer to a directory satisfies it fully. The committed-data design was solving a problem the consumer already solves with its lock.

**Benefits**

- **Scope drops by more than half.** No scheduled workflow, no Release uploads, no idempotency checks, no issue automation, no changed-source policy. What remains is fetch, cache, parse, derive, validate, and a CLI.
- **No growing history.** The no-floor spread layer is tens of MB per cutoff per month. Anyone cloning or pinning the repo would pay for all of it forever. The weight-floor question largely disappears.
- **Any month on demand.** Older regulations and other formats need no ingestion decision. The regulation registry becomes optional shortcuts rather than a gate.
- **Cleaner on licensing.** The public repo redistributes code, not bulk derived Smogon data.
- **Pin matters less.** The core output, stat points plus nature plus weight, does not depend on a Showdown commit. Derived final stats become an optional flag for consumers without their own stat engine. The consumer here has one and does not need them.

**Downsides**

- **Reproducibility leans on Smogon.** Results are reproducible only if the file at that URL never changes and stays reachable. Smogon has re-uploaded stats after pipeline fixes before, rarely. Mitigation: the generator writes a manifest with the raw file's sha256 and size, and the consumer's lock carries that hash. A silent change becomes a detected bump instead of a mystery. If you want insurance, add a manual `archive` command later that stashes the gzipped raw file somewhere of yours, but I would not build it until a file actually changes.
- **Network at generation time.** Fine as long as generation is not on the launch path.
- **Every consumer re-parses.** A 19 MB JSON parses in seconds. Not a concern.
- **No GitHub browsing of the data.** That was a nice-to-have in the spec, not a need.

**On "a generation step before launch."** I would move it one step earlier. Generate at bump time, commit the small locked export in the consumer, and have launch read that lock with no network and no generator involved. That matches how the team pool is already handled there, keeps every analysis result tied to a hash you own, and means a Smogon outage or a laptop offline never blocks a run. The generator supports this with a local cache for raw files keyed by month, format and cutoff, plus a flag to read a raw file from a path for offline reruns.

**What changes in the spec.** The output layout becomes a target directory rather than `data/`, the manifest becomes per-generation, the whole schedule and operations section is replaced by a CLI and library contract, and the acceptance tests keep fixture parse, Showdown-parity stats, byte-identical reruns, normalization invariants and schema validation while dropping the Release and manifest-integrity checks. Schemas stay, since they are still the contract.

Yes. The consumer's design was written for exactly this shape, and the handoff keeps this repo off every hot path. Here is how they fit.

**The handoff.** The consumer's plan already says: pin the chaos reader as a submodule by SHA, run its own exporter to write one small locked JSON per format and month, and have the belief-root builder read that lock once per root. With a generator instead of committed data, the only change is that the exporter runs the generator first. The chain becomes:

1. Monthly bump on the consumer side: run the generator for the chosen format and cutoff, hand its output to the exporter, commit the lock with the raw file's hash and the generator's SHA. This is a teams-style bump, recorded once.
2. At runtime: the belief-root builder reads the lock, filters a foe's entries to the sheet's nature and the engine's revealed Speed set, enumerates the top few spreads as worlds with their weights, and falls back to the uniform draw below a usage floor. No network, no generator, no parsing.

Three facts from the consumer's code make this thin:

- **Species ids match already.** The engine's tables are generated with Showdown's own id function, which is what this spec uses. The "in the engine's ids" mapping is the identity for species.
- **The Speed filter is in stat points.** The engine's revealed set is a list of allowed Speed points, not final stats. The generator's core output, nature plus six points plus weight, is exactly the shape consumed. Derived final stats are not needed downstream.
- **The world weights are enumerated, not sampled.** The search cost per root does not depend on how many spreads the lock holds. A fat lock is a few more bytes read once.

## Why it is not a bottleneck

There are three timescales where this could bind, and it binds on none of them.

- **Per search root:** nil. One dictionary lookup per foe entry on a file already in memory.
- **The build critical path:** the usage setting must land before the confidence-flag step, and the search core already takes a weight per world. What that step needs from this repo is one thing: a correct spread layer for one month, one format, one cutoff. The minimal generator delivers that without the schedule, Releases or summary percentiles.
- **Monthly cadence:** loosely coupled by design. If Smogon is late, or you do not get to the bump, the lock stays on last month and nothing breaks. If Smogon republishes a file, the raw hash in the generator's manifest differs from the lock's, and the bump reports it instead of silently moving numbers.

The Showdown pin stops being a coupling point at all. The core output needs no Dex. Load the pinned Showdown only for the optional derived-stats flag and for name validation. Then a regulation rotation never forces a generator release before the consumer can bump.

## What to get right in the generator for this to hold

- **Byte-identical output** for the same raw file, so the lock hash is stable across machines.
- **Raw source hash and size** in the generation manifest, carried into the lock.
- **Per-species totals** in the index, for the usage-floor fallback.
- **Spreads grouped or sortable by nature**, since the first filter downstream is the sheet's nature.
- **Any format and cutoff on the command line.** Which rating band to trust for Bo3 is the consumer's call, and it may want a Bo1 cutoff for its larger sample.
- **Offline input from a local raw file**, so a bump can be reproduced later without the network.
- **A local cache keyed by month, format and cutoff**, so repeated runs do not refetch.

The remaining genuine risk is historical availability. If Smogon ever removed a month, the lock would still work but could not be regenerated. That is acceptable today. A manual archive command for the raw gzip can be added the first time it matters.

# vgc-usage-stats — Specification

Status: **Draft** (revised 2026-10-13; first draft 2026-10-06). This document is
the source of truth for what the repo does. The implementation plan is built from
this file; change the spec first, then the code.

**2026-10-13 revision:** the repo is a **generator**, not a dataset. It no longer
commits derived data, runs on a schedule, or archives raw files. A consumer runs
it on demand for a month, format and cutoff, and keeps the output wherever it
wants. See §12 for what changed and why.

## 1. Purpose and consumers

Take one of Smogon's monthly Pokémon Showdown usage stats files for a VGC format
and turn it into a spread-level dataset on disk: for every species, every
reported spread as nature plus stat points plus weight, with optional derived
stats and summaries.

This is a standalone public tool. It is not built around any particular
downstream project; consumers adapt to its published output contract.

Consumers:

- **Downstream tools in any language** (TypeScript, Python, etc.), such as set
  inference, opponent modelling or damage-calc tooling. They run the CLI (or call
  the library from TypeScript) and read the JSON it writes. The output contract is
  language-neutral JSON with published JSON Schemas (§4.6).
- **People** exploring a month's spreads locally, through `summary.json`.

The expected consumer pattern is **generate once, then lock**: a consumer runs the
generator when it wants a new month, records the generation manifest's source
hash and this repo's commit alongside whatever it derives, and never runs the
generator at its own runtime. The generator is designed so that this is enough to
reproduce a result later (§6.5).

## 2. Source data (Smogon)

Root: `https://www.smogon.com/stats/`. Months are `YYYY-MM/` directories, from
2014-11 to the present. A few directories carry suffixes (`-DLC1`, `-H1`/`-H2`),
and none of them matter for Champions formats. A new month appears around the 1st
of the following month (2026-09 was published 2026-10-01).

Each month contains top-level usage `.txt` files plus `chaos/`, `moveset/`,
`leads/`, `metagame/` and `monotype/`. File names are
`<showdown-format-id>-<cutoff>.<ext>`.

**This repo reads `chaos/<format>-<cutoff>.json` only.** The `moveset/` text files
truncate spreads to the top ~6 plus an "Other" bucket (84% "Other" for Rillaboom
in regmc-1760), so they are never used, not even as a fallback.

### 2.1 Chaos JSON shape (as observed)

```jsonc
{
  "info": {
    "metagame": "gen9championsvgc2026regmc",
    "cutoff": 1760,
    "cutoff deviation": 0,
    "team type": null,
    "number of battles": 1631943
  },
  "data": {
    "Rillaboom": {
      "Raw count": 1410840,
      "Viability Ceiling": [58135, 84, 74, 62],
      "Abilities": { "grassysurge": 5995.33, ... },
      "Items":     { "miracleseed": ..., ... },
      "Spreads":   { "Adamant:32/32/0/0/2/0": 265.09, ... },  // Nature:HP/Atk/Def/SpA/SpD/Spe
      "Moves": { ... }, "Tera Types": { "nothing": ... }, "Happiness": { "255": ... },
      "Teammates": { ... }, "Checks and Counters": { ... },
      "usage": 0.4659939
    }
  }
}
```

In Champions formats the six spread numbers are **stat points (SP)**, not EVs:
0–32 per stat and at most 66 in total.

## 3. Inputs

The generator takes its inputs on the command line (§6). There is no committed
registry of regulations or formats; any format id Smogon publishes a chaos file
for is accepted.

- `--month YYYY-MM` (required).
- `--format <showdown-format-id>` (required, repeatable), e.g.
  `gen9championsvgc2026regmcbo3`.
- `--cutoff <n>` (required, repeatable), e.g. `0 1500 1630 1760`. Every
  format × cutoff pair is generated.
- `--raw <path>`: read a local chaos file instead of fetching (one format × cutoff
  per invocation). Used for offline reruns and tests.
- `--out <dir>` (required): the target directory (§4.1).
- `--cache <dir>`: where fetched raw files are kept (§6.3). Defaults to
  `~/.cache/vgc-usage-stats`.
- `--stats`: also derive final stats with the pinned pokemon-showdown (§5.2).
- `--summary`: also write `summary.json` (§4.3).
- `--min-share <x>`: drop spreads below this share of the species' total weight
  (§4.4). Default `0` (keep everything).

Regulations can overlap: 2026-06 had both regma and regmb chaos files. That is the
consumer's concern; the generator processes whatever it is asked for.

## 4. Outputs

### 4.1 Layout

Everything is written under `--out`:

```
<out>/
  <YYYY-MM>/
    <format>-<cutoff>/                    # e.g. gen9championsvgc2026regmcbo3-1760/
      manifest.json                       # §4.5, one per generation
      index.json                          # §4.2
      summary.json                        # §4.3, only with --summary
      spreads/
        <speciesid>.json                  # §4.4, one per species
```

`<speciesid>` is the Showdown ID (`toID(name)`): lowercase, alphanumerics only.
For example `Salamence-Mega` becomes `salamencemega`. This needs no Dex; it is a
string transform of the chaos key.

Rerunning into the same `--out` overwrites the format × cutoff directory. Nothing
is written if the run fails (§5.4): outputs go to a temporary sibling directory
and are moved into place at the end.

### 4.2 `index.json`

One per format/cutoff/month. Small; it lets consumers discover what exists.

- `schema_version`, `month`, `format`, `cutoff`
- `source`: Smogon URL (or the `--raw` path), `sha256` and `bytes` of the raw
  file as read
- `info`: the chaos `info` block, passed through unchanged
- `species`: an array of `{ name, id, file, total_weight, raw_count, usage,
  n_spreads }`, sorted by `total_weight` descending. `file` is relative, e.g.
  `spreads/rillaboom.json`.

`total_weight` and `raw_count` are what a consumer uses to decide whether a
species has enough data to trust (a usage floor is the consumer's choice).

### 4.3 `summary.json` (with `--summary`)

All species in one file, with no per-spread rows. Everything here is computed from
**all** spreads in the chaos file; `--min-share` does not apply.

Per species:

- `name`, `id`, `total_weight`
- `nature_share`: `{ [nature]: weight / total_weight }`, for natures with
  non-zero weight only. Exact, because the chaos spread list is complete (§9).
- `concentration`: `{ [nature]: { top1, top5 } }`. `top1` and `top5` are the
  weight of the 1 and 5 heaviest spreads within that nature, divided by that
  nature's total weight.
- `sp`: one block for `overall` and one per nature, `{ overall: StatBlock,
  by_nature: { [nature]: StatBlock } }`, where `StatBlock = { [stat]: Dist }`
  for `hp, atk, def, spa, spd, spe`, over **stat points**. Always present.
- `stats`: the same shape over **derived final stats**. Only with `--stats`.
- `Dist` has these fields:
  - `distribution`: `[{ value, weight, cum }]` sorted by `value` ascending. `value`
    is the integer stat points (or final stat), `weight` is the total spread
    weight producing that value, and `cum` is the cumulative weight fraction (0
    to 1). **This is the source of truth.**
  - Convenience fields: `p5, p10, p25, p50, p75, p90, p95, min, max, mean`.
  - **Percentile definition:** nearest rank on the discrete distribution. `pK` is
    the smallest `value` whose `cum ≥ K/100`, with no interpolation. `mean` is the
    weighted mean.

### 4.4 `spreads/<speciesid>.json`

The full spread layer for one species. **This is the primary output.**

- `schema_version`, `month`, `format`, `cutoff`, `name`, `id`, `total_weight`
- `min_share`: the floor applied, or `0`
- `dropped`: `{ count, weight }`, the spreads removed by the floor. The invariant
  is `kept weight + dropped.weight == total_weight`.
- `spreads`: an array sorted by `weight` descending, then `spread` ascending as a
  tiebreak. Each entry is:
  - `spread`: the original key, e.g. `"Adamant:32/32/0/0/2/0"`
  - `nature`
  - `sp`: `{ hp, atk, def, spa, spd, spe }`, stat points. **Pin-free:** true
    for the month regardless of any game-data version.
  - `weight`: the raw chaos weight
  - `share`: `weight / total_weight`
  - `stats`: `{ hp, atk, def, spa, spd, spe }`, derived final stats (§5.2).
    Only with `--stats`; tied to the manifest's `showdown_sha`.
- `by_nature`: `{ [nature]: [indices into spreads] }`, so a consumer that knows
  the nature (an open team sheet) can filter without a scan.

### 4.5 `manifest.json` (per generation)

- `schema_version`, `month`, `format`, `cutoff`, `generated_at`
- `generator`: `{ version, commit }`: this repo's package version and git SHA
  when available
- `showdown_sha`: the full pokemon-showdown commit used for derivation, or `null`
  without `--stats`
- `options`: `{ stats, summary, min_share }`
- `source`: `{ url | path, fetched_at, http_last_modified, http_etag, sha256,
  bytes }`. HTTP fields are `null` for `--raw`.
- `outputs`: for each file written, `{ path, sha256, bytes }`
- `quality`: `{ species, spreads_parsed, spreads_rejected,
  spreads_dropped_by_floor, weight_dropped_by_floor, max_rel_weight_mismatch,
  unresolved_species }`. `max_rel_weight_mismatch` is the largest relative
  difference, across species, between Σspreads and Σabilities. Any rejection
  fails the run (§5.4), so `spreads_rejected` is always 0 in a written manifest.

A consumer that records `source.sha256`, `generator.commit`, `options` and
`showdown_sha` can reproduce the outputs byte for byte (§6.5).

### 4.6 Schemas and versioning

- Every output file carries `schema_version` (semver).
- `schemas/` holds JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) files for `index`, `summary`,
  `spreads` and `manifest`. These schemas are the contract with consumers.
- A breaking change bumps the major version and is recorded in `CHANGELOG.md`.
  Consumers regenerate when they want the new version; nothing is migrated.

## 5. Derivation

### 5.1 Weights

A chaos weight is a rating-weighted team count. For a species,
`Σ Spreads = Σ Abilities = Σ Items = Σ Happiness = total_weight`, which also
equals `Raw count × Avg. weight` (the "Avg. weight" shown in the moveset header).
Shares are always normalized against that species' `total_weight`. Raw weights
are kept unchanged in the spread layer.

### 5.2 Final stats (`--stats` only)

- Use pokemon-showdown's own Champions stat calculation at the pinned SHA (§7):
  the `champions` mod's `statModify`, Level 50, without Level Clause Mod. At
  Showdown commit `9fb3a5b99f1a0bea17f495c5cc1bfe04fdd19c3e` (where it was
  verified, §9), that code is:
  - HP = `base + SP + 75`
  - Other stats = `trunc(trunc((base + SP + 20) × natureMult × 100, 16) / 100)`,
    where `natureMult` is 1.1 for the boosted stat, 0.9 for the lowered stat and 1
    otherwise (Showdown applies the nature with 16-bit truncation)
- Base stats come from the pinned Dex, resolved with the `champions` mod for the
  chaos species name, including formes and Megas.
- The implementation is a local function proven equal to Showdown by the
  acceptance test (§11.2), not a call into a running Battle (§10, D5).
- Out of scope: items, abilities, field effects and stat stages (§8).

Base stats change between game-data versions (Champions receives balance
patches), so derived stats are only meaningful together with `showdown_sha`.
Consumers with their own stat engine should recompute from `sp` at their own pin.

### 5.3 Spread parsing

Each `Nature:a/b/c/d/e/f` key must meet all of the following:

- The nature is one of the 25 natures.
- There are exactly six integers.
- Each value is between 0 and 32.
- The sum is at most 66.

Anything else is a rejection, recorded in `quality` (§5.4).

### 5.4 Failure policy

- A rejected spread fails the run.
- A weight mismatch above `1e-9` relative fails the run.
- A species name that does not resolve in the pinned Dex **fails the run with
  `--stats`** and is only **counted** (`quality.unresolved_species`) without it,
  since the core output needs no Dex. This keeps the core path usable when a new
  regulation adds species the pin does not know yet.
- The generator never falls back to `moveset/*.txt`.
- On failure nothing is written under `--out` and the exit code is non-zero.

## 6. Command line and library contract

### 6.1 Commands

```
vgc-usage-stats generate --month 2026-09 \
  --format gen9championsvgc2026regmcbo3 --cutoff 1760 \
  --out ./usage [--stats] [--summary] [--min-share 0] [--cache DIR]

vgc-usage-stats generate --raw ./chaos.json --month 2026-09 \
  --format gen9championsvgc2026regmcbo3 --cutoff 1760 --out ./usage

vgc-usage-stats list --month 2026-09 [--filter champions]
```

- `generate` is the product. It fetches (or reads `--raw`), parses, derives,
  validates against the schemas, runs the invariant checks (§11) and writes.
- `list` prints the chaos files Smogon has for a month, so a consumer can
  discover format ids and cutoffs. Read-only; it never writes to `--out`.
- Exit codes: `0` success; `2` bad arguments; `3` the month or file does not
  exist at Smogon (not an error for a month not yet published, but reported);
  `4` a fetch failed after retries; `5` a validation or invariant failure.

### 6.2 Library

The TypeScript package exports the same steps as functions, so a TypeScript
consumer need not shell out: fetch (with cache), parse, derive, summarize,
validate, write. The CLI is a thin layer over them. Python and other consumers
use the CLI and read the files.

### 6.3 Cache

Fetched raw files are stored gzipped under `--cache` as
`<month>/<format>-<cutoff>.json.gz` with a sidecar recording the URL, ETag,
Last-Modified and sha256. A later run for the same month, format and cutoff
reads the cache and does not touch the network unless `--refresh` is given. A
`--refresh` fetch that returns different bytes is reported on stderr with both
hashes, then used; the old file is kept as `.prev` until the next refresh.

### 6.4 Retries

HTTP: 3 attempts per file with exponential backoff, on 5xx responses, timeouts
and network errors. There is no outer retry; the consumer decides when to run
again.

### 6.5 Determinism and reproducibility

- The same raw bytes, generator commit, options and Showdown pin produce
  byte-identical outputs on any machine (stable key order, fixed number
  formatting, sorted arrays, no timestamps outside `manifest.json`).
- `manifest.json` is the only file with run-dependent fields (`generated_at`,
  `fetched_at`, HTTP headers). Everything a consumer needs to pin is in it.
- Reproducing an old generation needs the raw file. The cache keeps it; a
  consumer that wants insurance against Smogon changing or removing a file keeps
  its own copy of the gzipped raw and reruns with `--raw`. The generator does not
  archive anything itself (§8).

## 7. Technology

- Node `>=22.18.0` and TypeScript. Tests use `node --test`, and scripts run TS
  directly with Node's type stripping.
- `pokemon-showdown` is an npm git dependency pinned by full commit SHA:
  `github:smogon/pokemon-showdown#<sha>`, with the lockfile committed. It is
  loaded only for `--stats` and name resolution; the core path never imports it.
  The initial pin is `9fb3a5b99f1a0bea17f495c5cc1bfe04fdd19c3e`, where §5.2 was
  verified (§10, D6). Bumps are deliberate: re-verify §5.2 at the new commit,
  rerun the parity test, and record the change in `CHANGELOG.md`.
- Other runtime dependencies are kept minimal: a JSON Schema validator (e.g. Ajv)
  and nothing for HTTP beyond `fetch`.

## 8. Non-goals

- **No committed data.** The repo holds code, schemas, fixtures and docs. Outputs
  live wherever the consumer puts `--out`.
- **No scheduled job, no Releases, no archive of raw files.** The consumer runs
  the generator when it wants a month. (A manual raw-archive command may be added
  if Smogon is ever seen to change or remove a published file.)
- Not a published package (npm or PyPI) for now, and no runtime API. Consumers
  pin the repo by commit.
- No replay crawling and no data from third-party sites. Smogon `/stats/` is the
  only source.
- No effective-stat modifiers: items, abilities, field effects, stat stages.
- No moveset/leads/metagame parsing, and no items/moves/teammates outputs (for
  now).
- No consumer-specific exports (id remapping, top-N selection, usage floors).
  Those belong downstream.

## 10. Decisions

Resolved with the 2026-10-13 revision; kept here for the record.

- **D1 — Missing chaos file:** fail with exit code 3, never fall back to `.txt`.
- **D2 — Weight floor:** none by default. `--min-share` is a share of the
  species' total weight, not an absolute weight, so rare species keep their
  spreads; the floor and what it dropped are recorded in every spreads file.
- **D3 — `nature_share` keys:** natures with non-zero weight only.
- **D4 — Republished source:** no longer a pipeline question. The cache keeps
  what was fetched; `--refresh` reports a changed file and the manifest's source
  hash lets a consumer notice.
- **D5 — Stat function:** a local implementation of §5.2, proven by the §11.2
  test against Showdown. Simpler than building a Battle to read stats from.
- **D6 — Initial Showdown pin:** `9fb3a5b`, where §5.2 was verified.
- **D7 — Generator, not dataset** (2026-10-13): see §12.
- **D8 — Showdown is optional at runtime:** the core output is stat points,
  which need no game data. The pin is loaded only for `--stats`.

## 11. Acceptance criteria

All of these are automated tests that run in CI on every push.

1. **Fixture parse.** A trimmed chaos fixture (`test/fixtures/`, a few species
   with a handful of spreads, including an invalid one) parses to a committed,
   hand-checked table of `{ species, nature, sp, weight, share }`, and the invalid
   spread is rejected.
2. **Derived stats match Showdown.** For a fixed sample of spreads, at least one
   per stat and including a boosted and a lowered stat for several species, a
   Mega and a forme, the derived stats equal what pokemon-showdown computes at the
   pinned SHA. The test builds a Champions Reg M-C team and reads the stats
   Showdown reports.
3. **Byte-identical rerun.** Generating twice from the same raw file into two
   directories produces identical files, `manifest.json` excepted, and the
   manifests differ only in `generated_at` and fetch fields.
4. **Offline equals online.** Generating with `--raw` on the cached file equals
   generating from the URL.
5. **Normalization invariants**, within `1e-9`:
   - `Σ nature_share = 1`.
   - Every `distribution` ends at `cum = 1`.
   - Percentiles are monotonic (`min ≤ p5 ≤ … ≤ p95 ≤ max`).
   - `kept + dropped weight = total_weight`.
   - Σspreads = Σabilities for every species.
   - `by_nature` indices partition `spreads`.
6. **JSON Schema validation.** Every file written validates against `schemas/`
   for its `schema_version`.
7. **Manifest integrity.** Every file listed in `outputs` exists with a matching
   sha256 and size, and `source.sha256` matches the raw file.
8. **Percentile definition.** A small synthetic distribution checks nearest-rank
   percentiles against hand-computed values.
9. **Failure leaves no output.** A run that fails validation writes nothing under
   `--out` and exits non-zero.

## 12. Why a generator (2026-10-13)

The 2026-10-06 draft committed derived data monthly from a scheduled workflow and
archived raw files on GitHub Releases. That was replaced because:

- **The data is big and grows.** A no-floor spread layer is tens of MB per
  format × cutoff per month. Anyone pinning the repo by commit would carry all of
  it forever, and the weight-floor decision was being forced by git size rather
  than by what consumers need.
- **Consumers lock their own derivative anyway.** A set-inference tool keeps a
  small locked file in its own tree with the source hash and generator commit.
  Committing the full output here duplicated that with worse economics.
- **Scope.** Scheduling, Releases, idempotency, issue automation and the
  republished-source policy were most of the operational surface and none of the
  value. The generator keeps fetch, parse, derive, validate and write.
- **Any month on demand.** Older regulations and other formats need no ingestion
  decision or registry entry.
- **Licensing hygiene.** The public repo redistributes code, not bulk derived
  Smogon data.

What was given up: a guaranteed replay of old months if Smogon changes or removes
a file. The cache and `--raw` cover the common case; a raw-archive command is the
documented fallback if it is ever needed (§8).
